corrected_draft.title: DHS Revokes Harvard’s Student Exchange Certification
corrected_draft.description_short: DHS revoked Harvard’s SEVP certification on May 22, 2025; a judge blocked the action the next day. This concerned university certification, not individual visa revocations.
corrected_draft.description_medium: On May 22, 2025, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem notified Harvard that DHS had revoked its Student and Exchange Visitor Program certification, effective immediately. Harvard filed suit the next day, and a federal judge issued a temporary restraining order blocking the action. The university-level certification dispute threatened its ability to host F- and J-visa students; it does not establish that dozens of individual student visas were revoked.
corrected_draft.description_long: On May 22, 2025, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem sent Harvard a letter revoking the university’s Student and Exchange Visitor Program certification, effective immediately. The letter cited Harvard’s response to an April 16 request for records concerning international students. Harvard filed suit and sought a temporary restraining order on May 23; a federal judge granted the request that day, blocking the administration from implementing the revocation while the case proceeded. Harvard’s international students made up about one-quarter of its student body, and the administration’s action threatened the university’s ability to host students and scholars in F- and J-visa categories. This was a university-level certification action. It should not be described as the revocation of dozens of individual students’ visas in May. Later presidential visa restrictions were separate actions and should be recorded separately if relevant. A later court filing records DHS’s May 28 notice of intent to withdraw the certification and a June 20 preliminary injunction against the May letter; the government later stipulated that it would not rely on the letter to revoke Harvard’s certification.
